quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane to use.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle share half a lane with you.
Pass the motorcycle while staying in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane to use.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles with the same road rights as other vehicles. Give motorcyclists a complete lane width. They need room to move safely, even if it looks like there is space to share.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting a highway, when following a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: What happens when you combine alcohol with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both can increase.
The effects of both can decrease.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both can increase.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can strengthen the effects of both. For example, one drink combined with a cold medicine might affect you like having several drinks.

questions.question: During a zipper merge at a construction zone, drivers should:

options.text: Stay in their lane until the merge point.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in their lane until the merge point.
questions.explanation: When you see a 'Lane closed ahead' sign, stay in your lane until you reach the merge point. Then take turns with other drivers to merge smoothly and safely into the open lane.

questions.question: Highway signs that warn about dangerous conditions are called:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to possible hazards ahead. Follow warning signs for your safety. Ignoring them could lead to an accident caused by your carelessness.

questions.question: There may be times when 10 mph is too fast to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Drive slower than the posted speed limit when conditions require it. Bad traffic, weather, or poor visibility may mean you need to drive as slow as 10 miles per hour.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Gives you time to react to surprises.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to surprises.
questions.explanation: To have enough time to react to other drivers' mistakes, leave plenty of space between your vehicle and all vehicles around you.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights direct you to. Not all crossings have these safety devices. It is illegal to go around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: ____ limit your focus, awareness, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only blood alcohol above the legal limit can
Even a tiny amount of alcohol can
Only blood alcohol above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a tiny amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your focus, awareness, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. No one can safely drive after drinking.

questions.question: You may use your horn when you:
questions.explanation: It is appropriate to use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. Sound it to warn other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let that traffic merge safely.

questions.question: You see flashing signals at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing signals, you must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs of a train, such as lowered gates or the sound of an approaching train.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing on the left is permitted from either direction.
Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.
Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only if you are in the lane with the broken line.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks and obey all signs and signals. Trains share the road with cars, bicycles, and pedestrians.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a highway and want to move left. What should you do?

options.text: Look in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.
Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.
Look in your side mirror for traffic and turn on your directional signal.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your rearview mirror, side mirror, and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that their mirrors cannot see.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes going in the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down by gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels go off the road, keep them off the pavement and slow down gently with the brakes. At a safe speed, turn the wheel to get back on the road. Do not jerk the steering wheel hard.

questions.question: Driving at night is:
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous. It is harder to see, headlights from other cars can blind you, and there are more tired or impaired drivers on the road.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, what should you use to show you are turning?
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers when you are turning.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may pass, even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means you can pass if it is safe. You must make sure no oncoming traffic is coming before you pass.

questions.question: What color are highway exit distance signs?
questions.explanation: Highway signs that show destinations and distances are green with white letters.

questions.question: Is it safe to use cruise control on snowy or icy roads if you reduce your speed?
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snowy or icy roads. Your tires may slip and you will lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.

questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit on hills. It is unsafe and illegal to pass on a hill where you cannot see far ahead.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards on the road ahead?

options.text: Look at the entire road and all sides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Keep your left foot on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all sides.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead and scan the whole road, including the sides. This helps you spot problems early and react safely.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between lanes is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: White broken lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the path is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be on the road ahead.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn others.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Drive in the right lane only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe distance gives you time to react without sudden braking, which could cause a crash behind you.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen because drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to stay safe.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light tells you that a steady red light is coming soon.

questions.question: What does the posted speed limit show?

options.text: The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed when road and weather conditions are good.
The maximum safe speed in all road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed when road and weather conditions are good.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the limit. When conditions are bad, you should slow down.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: No one can pass from either direction.
Anyone can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass from either direction. You can only cross them to turn left or to pass pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter riders when the other lane is clear and safe.

questions.question: An oncoming car is on your left and a bicyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: When you have multiple hazards, handle one at a time. Do not try to pass the bicyclist while the car is coming toward you. Let the car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.question: It is illegal to drive too close to a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Driving too close to a motorcycle is illegal and dangerous. Never drive next to a motorcycle in the same lane.

questions.question: You must signal every time you pull away from a curb.
questions.explanation: You must use a turn signal every time you pull away from a curb.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also coming to the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, give the right-of-way to others, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: What must a driver do at a flashing red traffic signal?
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop, give the right-of-way, and go only when safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices turn off before going.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep driving at your current speed.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up.

questions.question: Two cars arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, you must give the right-of-way to a vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Leaving the car running in the driveway.

questions.explanation: Every time you stop quickly, you use fuel to speed back up. If you look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking, you will use less gas.
